previous_per_cell_budget_preserved_verba.meaning: --budget on cell.py is the per-cell REQUEST budget enforced at the 3/7 budget preflight: it takes the runner's own --dry-run would_send_total, multiplies by (1 + BUDGET_HEADROOM=0.10, cell.py:140), and refuses with Abort(3, '3/7 budget') when required > --budget (cell.py:388-392). It is not a runtime ceiling and it does not raise any cap.
previous_per_cell_budget_preserved_verba.arithmetic: turns 48 + rounds 48 = 96 (non-compact arms; cells 1-6, 9-10). transcript-compact cells (7, 8) add expected_digests=2 -> 98. Digests do NOT need adding to the non-compact figure; they are the only extra term and they exist only on the two compact cells.
previous_per_cell_budget_preserved_verba.gate_arithmetic: the shipped 10% headroom means the cell's --budget must exceed the raw projection: ceil(96 x 1.10) = ceil(105.6) = 106 for non-compact; ceil(98 x 1.10) = ceil(107.8) = 108 for transcript-compact.
previous_per_cell_budget_preserved_verba.recommended_reason: one uniform value covering all 10 cells (worst case = transcript-compact, 108). 106 would pass cells 1-6 and 9-10 and refuse cells 7-8.

wiring_consistency_check.requested: verify that --fetch-followup-allowance sets the per-arm rounds (run_longrun.py:226, :940-950) and that --budget is the per-cell request budget
wiring_consistency_check.result: DIVERGENT on the first premise, PARTLY DIVERGENT on the second
wiring_consistency_check.premise_1: --fetch-followup-allowance does NOT set the per-arm rounds. run_longrun.py:226 is a module constant with no override; run_longrun.py:940 compares against that constant. The flag is cell.py's G1 accounting reserve and never reaches the runner (cell.py:1550 argv).
wiring_consistency_check.premise_2: --budget IS the per-cell request budget, but it is a preflight gate with a 10% headroom applied to the runner's own projection (cell.py:388-392); it is not the ceiling the runner raises BudgetExhausted against.
wiring_consistency_check.paths_note: the card cited run_longrun.py:226 and :940-950 without a directory; the file is experiments/ptr-engine/longrun/run_longrun.py, not experiments/ptr-engine/measure/run_longrun.py (which does not exist)
wiring_consistency_check.consequence: raising the flag to 48 rescues the PRICE accounting (G1 reserves 96 instead of 72) but does NOT keep a channel open past 24 billed rounds. The 48-round half of this measurement is blocked on the frozen runner.

cards_that_must_read_this_file: orchestration/units/RUN-A-STAR.md (any card that launches the 10-cell grid)

what_48_does_not_fix.burst: a model that buys 21 rounds in one turn (v5 T3) can still buy 21 of 48; two such turns close it. What bounds it is the per-turn cap --fetch-rounds-per-turn (TOOL_FETCH_ROUNDS_PER_TURN = 3, run_longrun.py:232), which already holds a single turn to 3 BILLED rounds - v5 predates that bound. 48 alone bounds the pool, not the burst rate.
what_48_does_not_fix.structure: only 144 rounds per arm (3 x 48 turns, the per-turn-cap ceiling) makes closure arithmetically impossible in a 48-turn cell; 144 costs 1,924 and leaves 1,268 of 3,192
what_48_does_not_fix.wiring: 48 rounds cannot be switched on at all through an existing flag (see per_arm_round_cap.flag_exists = false)

previous_revision_preserved.answer_to_the_card_question: No, not with today's wiring: a 48-turn tools-on cell keeps its channel open only to 24 billed rounds (run_longrun.py:226), and the flag this unit was asked to set is an accounting reserve that does not reach the runner. With run_longrun.py:226 raised to 48 it would carry 48 rounds - 28 more than v6's observed 20 - but that is a demand margin, not a structural guarantee.

Over 16 cells that basis is 16 x 96 = 1,536, i.e. 1,128 + 1,536 = 2,664 cumulative, leaving 1,656. All three figures (1,056 / 1,108 / 1,536) fit the 4,320 cap; the brake cannot choose between them.
